To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) regular treatment with inhaled salbutamol for 28 days caused a significant reduction in bronchodilator response to salbutamol in patients with asthma, which was more evident in those patients with greater baseline bronchoconstriction; and 2) the magnitude of bronchodilatation was linearly related to the magnitude of bronchial hyperresponsiveness, such that patients with more severe baseline hyperresponsiveness had greater bronchodilator attenuation.
